correctness.rationale: Checked the reduction and certificate in RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md, verify.py and verification_output.txt without executing the uploaded code. The one-bit condition permits normalization to words starting in 0 and ending in 1. At n≥14 the seven-bit endpoint blocks are disjoint, so the maximum is the largest compatible rectangle size times 2^(n−14); this includes the boundary n=14 and self-pairs. In the submitted search the product of the largest possible prefix count and current compatible suffix count is a valid upper bound. At equal depth and suffix mask the greater chosen count dominates every continuation, so memoization is valid. Independently, `python3 /workspace/replay/restricted_overlap_closed_sets.py 1 2 3 4 5 6 7` constructed the graph by literal string comparisons and enumerated mutual closures without objective pruning. Any positive rectangle can be enlarged to a mutually closed one; each nonroot closed prefix set is reachable by adding its least not-yet-included element and closing, with the canonical test rejecting additions inducing lower new indices. This traversed 1,944 closed sets with nonempty suffix side at cutoff seven, found maximum 744 with a 24×31 witness, and returned the sequence 1,2,6,20,64,216,744 across all seven cutoffs. A separate intersection-state dynamic program confirmed 744 and checked the frozen witness directly. These exact finite computations establish the endpoint coefficient only; the disjoint-block argument extends it to all stated n.

evidence: The bound reproduced by Stanovnik, (q^n−q^(n−k))/(2k), gives about 1161.14 at q=2,k=7,n=14. The bound in the inspected Yang–Ding §5 is for a specified constructed family under extra conditions. The Cai–Wang–Feng paper was not accessible; the improved general bound and reduction attributed to it by Stanovnik do not yield 744.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A weaker bound leaves open the 744 maximum. A bound on a specified family is not an upper bound on the unrestricted class. Unread constructions or bounds in Cai–Wang–Feng cannot be assessed from the secondary citation alone.

evidence: Blackburn et al. formulate the endpoint incidence problem and construct the 24×31 rectangle. Stanovnik gives S₁ᵏ(q,n)=q^(n−2k)S₁ᵏ(q,2k), with a factorization for more general overlap ranges.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An unrestricted prefix/suffix biclique product at n=2k is the exact reduced invariant, so its 744 evaluation would cover every n≥14. The equivalence and its blocklength factor are themselves prior, but they do not determine the best rectangle.

originality.rationale: Best of current evidence, the claimed distinct contribution is solely the unrestricted binary matching upper bound at cutoff seven. The witness, the compatibility-graph viewpoint and the middle-word scaling already occur in the literature. The strongest available same-parameter sources leave the coefficient gap open; an inaccessible plausible source remains a named risk, not negative evidence.
residual_risks: The Cai–Wang–Feng full paper was unavailable; only its bound and reduction as described in Stanovnik could be assessed. Historical priority against additional theorems in that paper or unindexed equivalent searches is not certified.

value.rationale: This is the next natural binary cutoff after the previously exact smaller cutoffs and a case explicitly treated as computationally difficult in the construction paper. Closing the real gap between its witness and upper bound fixes the capacity for every n≥14, rather than reporting one experiment or recomputing a known table entry. The exact endpoint calculation is reproducible and avoids assuming that a specially constructed family contains an unrestricted optimum.
